title: Anthropic likely to price IPO above the current range of $70 to $78
content:
Anthropic is likely to price its IPO above the current range of $70 to $78, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
The artificial intelligence company is planning to close the order books and lock in total demand at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Anthropic is slated to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" and start trading on Nov. 19.
If Anthropic's IPO proceeds as planned, the company will debut roughly five months after SpaceX went public in a record offering that raised $85.7 billion. But Anthropic is facing a public market that's grown increasingly skeptical of the AI trade, as well as mounting and widespread antipathy toward the technology in the U.S.
A group of researchers, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, co-founded the company in 2021 after defecting from OpenAI, now its chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, and it underwent a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic has long worked to establish a reputation as a safety-conscious AI company, and its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its listing.
"I think if we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia," Amodei said in Anthropic's roadshow video. "We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways that things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time."
"I invite you to join us on the next phase of this journey," Amodei said.

report.summary: Anthropic is expected to price its IPO above the $70–$78 range, listing on Nasdaq as ANT after explosive Claude Code-driven revenue growth.
report.background: Anthropic was founded in 2021 by researchers who left OpenAI, including CEO Dario Amodei, and became best known for its Claude family of AI models. The company’s 2026 growth was driven largely by Claude Code, its AI coding tool, which helped revenue surge. Its IPO arrives roughly five months after SpaceX’s record listing, but in a public market increasingly skeptical of the AI trade and amid broader public antipathy toward the technology. Anthropic has positioned itself as safety-conscious, yet its prospectus includes more than 90 pages of risk factors, underscoring both the opportunities and controversies surrounding the listing.
key_points: Anthropic is likely to price its IPO above the stated $70–$78 range, with order books expected to close Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. The company plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT” and begin trading Nov. 19, roughly five months after SpaceX’s record IPO.

For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic reported $33.24 billion in revenue, up about 1,200% year over year. It posted a $104 billion net loss, mostly from fair-value changes on convertible notes and derivative liabilities, compared with a $25.1 billion loss in the same stretch of 2025.

Anthropic’s explosive 2026 growth was driven largely by Claude Code, its AI coding tool, which became a breakout product. The company is best known for its Claude model family, and its roadshow leans heavily on both business momentum and its long-standing safety-focused identity.

The IPO faces a tougher market backdrop: investors have grown more skeptical of AI valuations, and the U.S. public mood toward AI is increasingly negative. Anthropic’s prospectus lists more than 90 pages of risk factors, and CEO Dario Amodei used the roadshow to acknowledge both AI’s potential benefits and its dangers.
report.impact: Anthropic’s IPO is a major test of public-market appetite for pure-play AI companies. A strong pricing above range would validate the AI business model and set a valuation benchmark for rivals such as OpenAI, while a weak debut could cool the AI funding frenzy. For developers, a public Anthropic brings more scrutiny, disclosure and capital, but also potential pressure on API pricing and product strategy; Claude Code’s ecosystem will be closely watched. Regular users may see AI tools become more mainstream and better funded, but safety claims and risk disclosures will face sharper investor and public attention. The listing also signals that AI’s biggest players now need to answer to public shareholders, not just private backers.
report.tools: Follow Anthropic’s official Claude API and Claude Code documentation for product updates. Developers can compare open-source coding agents such as Aider, Cline and Continue, which offer alternatives to proprietary workflows. Investors and researchers should read Anthropic’s SEC prospectus, especially its risk factors and financial notes, to understand the IPO’s structure and losses.
